title: Gaussian two-point bound below the midpoint
statement: Let $a,b\in\mathbb R$ satisfy $b\ge0$, $a-b>0$, $a+b<1$, and $a\le\frac12$. For the Gaussian isoperimetric profile $U$, one has $U(a)\le\frac{\sqrt{U(a+b)^2+b^2}+\sqrt{U(a-b)^2+b^2}}{2}$.
replaced: Let $\Phi$ and $\varphi$ be the standard Gaussian distribution function and density, and put $Q=\Phi^{-1}$ and $I(p)=\varphi(Q(p))$ for $0<p<1$. If $b\ge0$, $a-b>0$, $a+b<1$, and $a\le1/2$, then $I(a)\le\bigl(\sqrt{I(a+b)^2+b^2}+\sqrt{I(a-b)^2+b^2}\bigr)/2$.
